inputs.drivers: Middle East flows; refinery outages; attacks on Russian infrastructure; product inventories; seasonal demand; crude-product dislocation.
inputs.invalidation: Rapid refinery restarts, weaker product demand, normalising crack spreads, or higher regulatory costs.
inputs.seed_claim: Crude markets may move toward surplus while gasoline, diesel, and refinery capacity remain tight, allowing refiners to benefit from elevated product cracks even if crude softens.
inputs.supporting_evidence: The seed cites IEA four-year-high product cracks and margins plus a rebound in VLO first-quarter refining income.
inputs.value_chain: Refiners; crack spreads; gasoline and diesel; crude oil.

objective: Research one crude-surplus and refining-tightness investment idea.
